submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 is recommended at 6 cm thickness to achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c while meeting all hard requirements. 

Radiator-R1 is eliminated because it fails the ageing requirement with 40% transparency loss (far exceeding the 10% limit). This is due to water uptake into its porous structure.

Between the remaining candidates (R2 and R3), Radiator-R3 is superior because:
1. It is a porous radiator with hydrophobic treatment, which should maintain a high refractive index (similar to R1) while solving the water uptake problem through the hydrophobic treatment
2. Higher refractive index provides better angular separation between pion and kaon Cherenkov rings
3. It passes the ageing test with only 6% transparency loss (well under the 10% limit)

Radiator-R2, while having excellent ageing performance (3% loss), is explicitly described as having "lower index", which would result in worse pion/kaon separation.

The 6 cm thickness is chosen as the maximum allowed value to maximize photon yield, which directly improves the Cherenkov angle resolution and thus the particle separation capability. This combination should provide the best possible pion/kaon separation while satisfying all constraints.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is listed in candidate_specs.md as 'porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment'

requirements.requirement: Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 with its high refractive index (porous structure with hydrophobic treatment) at maximum thickness (6 cm) provides the best separation performance. The high index maximizes the difference in Cherenkov angles between pion and kaon, and the maximum thickness maximizes photon yield for best angular resolution.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Ageing tests show Radiator-R3 has 6% transparency loss at 400 nm, which is below the 10% limit. The hydrophobic treatment prevents water uptake into the porous structure.
Recommended thickness is 6 cm, which is at the upper bound of the allowed range [1, 6] cm

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 at 6 cm thickness provides the optimal combination: highest refractive index among viable candidates (R1 is excluded due to ageing failure) and maximum thickness for photon yield, resulting in the best achievable separation performance
